title: Canonical continuous coefficient module equivalences in the scheme universe
statement: Let $X:\mathrm{Scheme}_u$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and abelian section groups in universe $u+1$. For a commutative topological ring $T:\mathrm{Type}_u$, write $\underline T(S)=C(S,T)$ for the condensed ring [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], $T_X=p_X^*\underline T$ for its pullback [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and $F_{X,T}(U)=\mathrm{ULift}_{u+1}C(|U|,T)$ for its continuous section-ring sheaf [def-sfb-continuous-lattice-coefficients]. Define $\operatorname{continuousSectionRingIso}_{X,T}:F^{\mathrm{lat,ring}}_{X,T}\simeq F_{X,T}$ to be the identity on sections, where $F^{\mathrm{lat,ring}}_{X,T}$ denotes the continuous coefficient sheaf after forgetting commutativity. If $T$ is totally disconnected, define the canonical equivalence from internal $T_X$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] to sheaves of $F_{X,T}$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] as follows: restrict the action along the inverse of the canonical adjoint comparison [def-sfb-continuous-ring-canonical-comparison], whose invertibility is [lem-sfb-continuous-ring-universe-realization]; apply the section-action equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]; then transport through the reconstructed-section-ring isomorphism of [def-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-module-encoding]. This is $\operatorname{continuousRingModuleEquivalenceUniverse}_{X,T}$. Composing with transport along $\operatorname{continuousSectionRingIso}_{X,T}$ gives $\operatorname{continuousLatticeModuleEquivalenceUniverse}_{X,T}$, with target the module sheaves over the underlying ring of the commutative continuous coefficient sheaf. Finally, for a prime $\ell$ and a normed field $E:\mathrm{Type}_u$ with a normed $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra structure [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], define $\operatorname{continuousFieldModuleEquivalenceUniverse}_{\ell,E,X}$ by this latter equivalence for $T=E$, using its induced ultrametric topology to supply total disconnectedness. No finite-dimensionality, completeness or geometric finiteness hypothesis is required. All coefficient transports are the specified canonical constructions, with their underlying additive section maps unchanged.
